in_text_mentions: nsional, color and pulsed Doppler echocardiography. M-mode tracing was used in case of arrhythmias and whenever necessary. The diagnosis of an atrioventricular septal defect relies on the following sonographic markers: (1) atrioventricular valves inserting into a common junction or in a linear fashion instead of the normal differential insertion; (2) a large defect “discontinuity” located in the cushion zone of the atrioventricular septum; (3) atrial and ventricular septal defects of varying size; (4) aorta “unsprung” from the crux of the heart; (5) unstable floating “kicking” crux (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: The parents opted for therapeutic abortion. The autopsy of the fetus showed ectopia cordis and multiple anomalies consistent with amniotic band disruption sequence [Figure 5]. The lower sternum was intact. The diaphragm and pericardium showed no defects. The fetal heart was dissected for further details. The intra-cardiac anatomy diagnosed by fetal echocardiography was confirmed on autopsy [Figure 6]. The atrioventricular orifice was guarded by a common AV valve which was dysplastic.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is the preoperative 3D TEE midesophageal short-axis diastolic view (atrial and ventricular perspective) from a real patient. The caption and in-text explicitly attribute it to a complete AVSD with two separate orifices of a common AV valve and no atrial component, directly matching the configured target disease. The common AV valve morphology is the textbook defining feature; the absent atrial component and trifoliate LAVV make this a less common (variant) form. No ethnicity, age, or skin findings are stated or assessable. B: Panel B is the corresponding systolic 3D TEE midesophageal short-axis view (atrial and ventricular perspective) from the same real patient. It shows the same common AV valve with two orifices and the superior bridging leaflet, directly supporting complete AVSD. The absent atrial component is a recognized less-common (variant) form. No ethnicity, age, or skin findings are stated or assessable.

panels.rationale: Single-panel cardiac MRI of a human patient (adult per article title and in-text 'survive into adulthood'). The image is annotated with mLA, mRA, RV, LV, Ao and an 'AVSD' label, and the caption explicitly states a complete atrioventricular septal defect with atrioventricular discordance; the in-text confirms CAVSD with a common atrioventricular valve. The panel is a real diagnostic imaging study of the configured target disease, so it is included. The combination with situs inversus, levocardia and double outlet right ventricle makes this an atypical presentation rather than a textbook isolated AVSD. [raw subtype: common atrioventricular valve (complete AVSD / CAVSD)]

panels.rationale: Single cardiac CT angiogram of a real pediatric patient with a history of surgical correction of complete atrioventricular septal defect. The caption documents enlarged right atrium, small right ventricle and a narrow (1.03 cm) tricuspid annulus, with an on-image caliper measurement of 10.3 mm; the small right ventricle corresponds to ventricular imbalance, the one configured finding directly supported. The image primarily depicts a late post-repair complication (tricuspid stenosis) rather than the primary defect anatomy, so confidence is moderate but the panel is a genuine patient radiology image attributable to the configured disease.
